newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lebed ouster won't change Russia-U.S. ties - Perry.
newsitem.headline: Lebed ouster won't change Russia-U.S. ties - Perry.

text.p: The sacking of Russian security chief Alexander Lebed will not change the "strong and growing" security ties between between Washington and Moscow, U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry said on Thursday.
"We should not be surprised that there are problems as Russia emerges as a democratic state," he told reporters. "We should be happy that they are handling those problems effectively."
"Any student of history that studies the first 10 years of the American emergence as a democratic nation will discover that there was a hell of a lot of turbulence in those first 10 years."

"The relationship between Mr Lebed and U.S. officials never really had a chance to develop, and so I don't see any fundamental change in the U.S.-Russian relationship in terms of this announcement," Perry added.
Perry said he had cancelled a meeting with Lebed at the last minute late on Thursday because he was aware of the problems that Lebed was having with the government.
"I could not forecast this particular outcome, but it seemed unwise to go ahead and schedule that meeting and so we did not schedule it," he told reporters in response to questions.

"The (U.S.-Russian) relationship at the defence ministers' level is strong and is growing. The relationship with the prime minister is strong and growing. The relationship between our presidents remains strong," Perry said.

"Our security relationship will proceed just as it has been proceeding," added Perry, who met Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov and other senior government officials, including Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, on Wednesday and Thursday.

U.S. Ambassador to Russia Thomas Pickering and U.S. Senators Richard Lugar of Indiana and Joseph Lieberman of Connecticut, both visiting Moscow with Perry, also voiced confidence in U.S.-Russian ties.
But Pickering also injected a note of caution regarding the well-publicised popularity of Lebed with many Russians.
"I think it is very important to see where the various pieces fall," he said. "Is Lebed still a major political force in Russian politics? I think time will tell us the answer to that question."

Democratic Senator Lieberman said Chernomyrdin had assured Perry and the U.S. delegation during a meeting on Thursday that he was in regular contact with President Boris Yeltsin and that "his (Yeltsin's) pace of activity was good."
"This is clearly an assertion that President Yeltsin is still very much in control," he said.
